Hi Anita — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise, auditable summary and I attached a short playbook excerpt and an ops snippet (territory-seal-playbook-v1.pdf, ops-runbook-snippet.txt).

High-level guarantees (Dedicated — US tenant):
- Data locality: All request payloads, model context (including KV cache persisted checkpoints), audit logs, and temporary artifacts are anchored to the customer’s US-dedicated tenant. Network egress is restricted to our US region boundary for that tenant.
- Snapshot/backup replication: For Dedicated tenants configured with "territory-seal", automated cross-region snapshot replication is disabled by default. Any manual replication requires a documented change request plus approvals from Redwood ops and legal.
- Wipe timeline and artifacts: Standard full-tenant wipe proceeds in phases: 1) delete live objects and KV checkpoints (minutes to hours depending on queue), 2) tombstone and mark snapshots for deletion (typically 24–72 hours to garbage-collect depending on underlying storage provider), 3) remove metadata entries and purge indices (up to 7 days for a conservative retention window we use for reviews). Evidence package we provide after completion: signed ops runbook excerpt, deletion log CSV (object keys + timestamps), snapshot manifest showing tombstone and final deletion markers, and an optional cryptographic hash summary of wiped snapshot IDs.
- Proof of non-replication: Our platform includes an immutable replication-audit log for each tenant; when "territory-seal" is active that log shows replication_disabled=true and records any attempted replication requests (none are permitted without change request). We include a trimmed sample audit log as part of the evidence package.

Operational contacts:
- Primary ops: Ben Carter (ben.carter@redwood.com) — runs tenant wipe procedures
- Escalation: Laura Bennett (laura.bennett@redwood.com) — Legal & Compliance liaison

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben to confirm low-level runbook steps and expected time windows.
2) We schedule a 30-min session (ops demo) to walk through executing a sandbox tenant wipe and viewing the evidence artifacts.
3) We stage a DocuSign for acceptance of the territory-seal configuration so procurement can push forward.

Ben, Laura — can you validate the timing and the exact artifacts in the attached playbook? Anita — I’ll hold a tentative slot tomorrow at 10:00am PT for the ops demo unless you prefer a different time.

> High-level guarantees (Dedicated — US tenant):

Technical details (ops-runbook highlights):
- KV checkpoint handling: KV cache checkpoints are flushed to tenant-scoped object storage and labeled with a tenant and region tag. Deletion begins with a forced KV tombstone that prevents any replay; tombstoned checkpoints are retained only long enough to ensure running in-flight requests complete (typically under 10 minutes) before collection begins.
- Snapshot lifecycle: Each snapshot entry has three flags: active, tombstoned, deleted. Garbage collection sweeps tombstoned entries and their blocks. In our Dedicated "territory-seal" config the storage tier for snapshots is region-local and cross-region replication is programmatically disabled (flag set on create).
- Backup/archival: Archived backups are stored on region-local cold storage. Retention policy on creation is set per contract; for wipe we trigger a retention-override flow with the storage provider to accelerate deletion and receive an expunge confirmation.
- Audit artifacts produced: deletion_log.csv (object_id, object_type, action, timestamp, operator_id), snapshot_manifest.json (list of snapshot ids + tombstone timestamps), replication_audit.log (entries showing replication_disabled=true), and a signed ops-execution.txt (operator, time, brief notes).
- Evidence delivery: Post-wipe we deliver a zipped evidence bundle (hashed and time-stamped) via a secure pre-authenticated download link. If you require, we can also produce a notarized statement signed by our ops lead.

Estimated durations (typical):
- Live object deletion and tombstone: immediate to a few hours (depends on queue).
- Snapshot garbage collection start: 24–72 hours after tombstone.
- Complete metadata purge/indices: up to 7 days (conservative upper bound).

We can run the sandbox demo tomorrow at 10:00am PT and perform a controlled wipe in a non-production tenant so you can watch the evidence package produced end-to-end.
